items.stem: Two events A and B are independent with P(A)=0.3 and P(B)=0.5. What is P(A and B)?

options.rationale: Correct: for independent events P(A and B)=P(A)P(B)=0.3x0.5=0.15.
0.80 is P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B) only under a different setup; it is the union-style sum, not the intersection.
0.50 is P(B) alone and ignores independence multiplication.
Independent events with positive probabilities have a positive joint probability.

items.explanation: Correct: for independent events P(A and B)=P(A)P(B)=0.3x0.5=0.15.

items.stem: For a continuous random variable, the expected value E[X] is best described as which of the following?

options.text: The integral of x times the probability density function over its support
options.rationale: Correct: E[X]=integral of x f(x) dx over the support for a continuous variable.

options.text: The most likely single value (the mode)
options.rationale: The mode is the density's peak, not the mean.

options.text: The middle value (the median) in all cases
options.rationale: The median equals the mean only for symmetric distributions, not in general.
The range is max minus min, unrelated to expectation.

items.explanation: Correct: E[X]=integral of x f(x) dx over the support for a continuous variable.

items.stem: Select TWO quantities that require the joint distribution of two random variables to compute. (Select TWO.)

options.text: The covariance of X and Y
options.rationale: Correct: covariance depends on the joint distribution of X and Y.

options.text: The correlation of X and Y
options.rationale: Correct: correlation is derived from covariance and thus the joint distribution.
The marginal mean of X needs only X's distribution.
The marginal variance of Y needs only Y's distribution.
The marginal median of X needs only X's distribution.

items.explanation: Correct: covariance depends on the joint distribution of X and Y.
